檢校 is an acting appointment, not a separate post of inspector, and 司馬 is the administrator of the princely establishment.

Emperor Ruizong's daughters, Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen, took religious vows; an edict directed that a monastery be built for each, and though it was the sweltering late summer, work on them never stopped.

Emperor Ruizong's daughters, Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen, entered the Daoist order; an edict directed that a Daoist abbey be built for each, and though it was the sweltering late summer, work on them never stopped.
入道 for these Tang princesses is entering the Daoist order, and 觀 is a Daoist abbey, not a Buddhist monastery.
Your Majesty is now building monasteries for the princesses, intending to accumulate merit and pray for divine protection.
Your Majesty is now building Daoist abbeys for the princesses, intending to accumulate merit and pray for divine protection.
造觀 is building Daoist abbeys. Monasteries renders 觀 as if it were a Buddhist institution.

I humbly pray that Your Majesty will heed the people's wishes, align with Heaven's intent, issue a gracious edict and clear policy, halt the labor at once, and let the people return to their homes and fields.
I humbly pray that Your Majesty will heed the people's wishes, align with Heaven's intent, issue a gracious edict and clear policy, halt the labor at once, and recover the loss before it is too late.
收之桑榆 is the idiom for retrieving a loss at the last moment, not sending the people home to mulberry trees and elms.

Trial appointees, supernumeraries, and acting inspectors in the various offices now number nearly two thousand; the grand treasury's cloth and silk are exhausted, and the grand granary can scarcely meet demand.

Trial appointees, supernumeraries, and acting inspectors in the various offices now number more than two thousand; the grand treasury's cloth and silk are exhausted, and the grand granary can scarcely meet demand.
二千餘人 is more than two thousand. Here 僅 means 'as many as,' so 'nearly two thousand' undercounts them.
Moreover, work on the Jinxian, Yuzhen, and other monasteries is none of it urgent; I memorialized earlier asking that it stop, yet it still has not.
Moreover, work on the Jinxian, Yuzhen, and other Daoist abbeys is none of it urgent; I memorialized earlier asking that it stop, yet it still has not.
觀 is a Daoist abbey. The idiomatic 'monasteries' makes the buildings Buddhist.

率府 is a guard command. 'Rate office' misreads 率 as the word for a rate.
If this evil long goes unreformed, your subject fears it will become an illness in the vital core; even Bian Que and Chunyu Yi could not cure it—how could it be merely a toenail ailment!
If this evil long goes unreformed, your subject fears it will become an illness in the vital core; even Physician He and Physician Huan could not cure it—how could it be merely a toenail ailment!
和 and 緩 are the Qin physicians Yi He and Yi Huan. The literal names Bian Que and Chunyu Yi, who are different men.
Achieving this good and ending that abuse is as easy as turning one's hand—why hesitate to act?
Achieving this good and ending that abuse is as easy as turning one's hand—why should Your Majesty be reluctant to act?
The Chinese addresses 陛下 directly. The idiomatic sentence drops Your Majesty, who is the person being asked to act.

It also says: "What you do not yet see, plan for."
不見是圖 means to plan for what is not yet visible. The idiomatic sentence reverses it into a ban on pursuing what is not right.
What have remote prefectures and frontier tribes done to deserve the court's reform, that they alone should suffer bad governors!
What wrong have small prefectures, distant commanderies, and tribal settlements done the sage's teaching, that they alone should suffer misgovernment?
何負於聖化 asks what offense they have given the sage's civilizing work. 'Deserve the court's reform' reverses the point.

Frontier regions where non-Chinese and Chinese peoples mix, dangerous and distant, are hard to govern—they depend all the more on upright officials to maintain order.
